entities.summary: Reginald Pole was the last Catholic Archbishop of Canterbury, holding the office from 1556 to 1558 during the Marian Restoration of Catholicism. A devout English cardinal, Pole was born in London and educated at Cambridge University, where he studied theology and became a prominent figure in the Catholic Church. His leadership during this period was marked by his efforts to restore Catholic practices and traditions in England, which had been largely abandoned during the Protestant Reformation. Pole's actions had significant consequences, including the exile of Protestant reformers and the imposition of Catholic rituals on English Catholics. Despite his efforts, Pole's tenure was cut short by his death on November 27, 1558. Reginald Pole's legacy continues to shape the complex and often contentious history of Catholicism in England, leaving a lasting impact on the country's religious landscape. The 1556 Marian Restoration of Catholicism, which Pole oversaw, had far-reaching effects on English society, including the persecution of Protestants and the suppression of dissenting voices. Pole's commitment to the Catholic Church and its traditions has been both celebrated and criticized by historians, who continue to debate the significance of his role in shaping England's religious history.
